title: Critters
tagline: They eat so fast, you don't have time to scream.
about: Furry alien convicts crash on a Kansas farm and start eating everything, with two shape-shifting bounty hunters tearing through town after them.
cue: Serve the Krite fritter balls when the Krites roll up to the house firing quills.

Hot honey wings, blue cheese dip.How to make it1kg chicken wings, tips off and jointed1 tbsp baking powder2 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp garlic powder60ml hot sauce3 tbsp honey30g butter100g blue cheese, crumbled125g sour cream2 celery sticks, cut in batonsPat the wings dry and toss with the baking powder, paprika, garlic powder and salt.Bake on a rack at 220°C, turning once, until crisp and cooked through.Melt the butter with the hot sauce and honey and toss the hot wings through it.Mash the blue cheese into the sour cream and serve with the wings and celery.Rolling Krite corn fritter ballsKrites roll up and fire quills. Spiky corn balls, chive sour cream.How to make it3 corn cobs, kernels cut off100g self-raising flour1 egg3 spring onions, sliced80g cheddar, grated100g plain corn chips, crushed250ml vegetable oil, for frying125g sour cream1 small bunch chives, snippedMix the corn, flour, egg, spring onions, cheddar and a pinch of salt into a stiff batter.Roll into walnut-size balls with wet hands, then roll them in the crushed corn chips so they come up spiky.Shallow-fry in batches in the hot oil, turning, until golden all over.Stir the chives through the sour cream and serve with the balls.Pickled eggs from the coopCheck the chicken's nest twice.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsHalf-eaten cow burnt endsKrites ate half the cow. Sticky beef ends.How to make it1.5kg beef brisket point2 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp smoked paprika2 tsp garlic powder1 tsp cracked black pepper250ml beef stock250ml smoky barbecue sauce2 tbsp honey1/4 green cabbage, shredded3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 tbsp apple cider vinegar4 soft white rollsRub the beef with the sugar, paprika, garlic powder, pepper and salt.Roast covered with the stock at 150°C until tender.Cut into 3cm cubes, toss with the barbecue sauce and honey and roast uncovered at 200°C until sticky and charred.Mix the cabbage with the mayo and vinegar.Serve the burnt ends with the slaw and rolls.Bowling alley chilli with cornbreadBowling alley panic. Smoky beef chilli.How to make it750g beef mince2 tbsp vegetable oil1 brown onion, diced3 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp chilli powder2 tsp ground cumin800g tinned crushed tomatoes400g tin kidney beans, drained150g fine cornmeal125g self-raising flour2 eggs250ml buttermilk80g butter, melted100g cheddar, gratedBrown the beef in the oil with the onion and garlic.Add the chilli powder and cumin, then the tomatoes and beans, and simmer gently until thick and dark.Whisk the cornmeal, flour, eggs, buttermilk, melted butter and a pinch of salt and pour into a lined 20cm tin.Bake at 200°C until golden and springy.Serve the chilli topped with cheddar and squares of buttered cornbread.TreatsBrown family buttermilk pancakesBreakfast before Charlie. Maple butter stack.How to make it225g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda2 tbsp caster sugar2 eggs375ml buttermilk60g butter, melted, plus 60g softened125ml maple syrup150g blueberriesWhisk the flour, baking powder, bicarb, sugar and a pinch of salt.Whisk the eggs, buttermilk and melted butter, then fold into the dry mix until just combined.Cook ladlefuls in a buttered pan until bubbles show, flip and cook until golden.Beat the softened butter with 2 tablespoons of the maple until fluffy and serve on the stack with the rest of the maple and the blueberries.DrinksCharlie's whiskey sourCharlie's bottle goes Molotov. Bourbon sour.How to make it240ml bourbon120ml fresh lemon juice80ml sugar syrup2 egg whites4 maraschino cherries2 cups ice cubesShake the bourbon, lemon, syrup and egg white hard without ice, then again with ice.Strain into 4 glasses and drop a cherry in each.Black coffee for CharlieCharlie hears messages in his fillings.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
